name: Earth-fault voltage relay
summary: Relay form that operates on a voltage appearing because of an earth fault, such as between a frame and earth.
description: This relay measures a voltage that appears only when there is an earth fault, for example between exposed metalwork and a reference earth, or across a neutral earthing impedance. It is useful where earth-fault current is limited and a voltage is easier to detect than a current.

The symbol does not say where the voltage is measured. A relay across a neutral earthing resistor and one connected between frame and auxiliary earth electrode have very different settings, so the measurement points must be drawn and labelled.
readingNotes: Trace both measurement connections of the relay.
Check the reference earth used by the relay.
distinction: An earth-fault voltage relay measures fault-related voltage; a residual voltage relay measures zero-sequence voltage from VT windings.
